passages.text: By 2007, law enforcement publicly acknowledged that the evidence had not developed into a prosecutable homicide case against him.
Any timeline should therefore describe Bowman as a person extensively investigated, not as the killer.
August 13, 2002: Bowman allegedly asked his landlord to help him move a mobile home and reportedly referred to a Virginia man who would not complete the job.
August 16, 2002: Bowman returned to speak with Lemons, reportedly left property behind, and then departed for Canada.
August 18, 2002: Lemons contacted investigators after learning about the Short murders and provided information about Bowman.
September 28, 2002: Authorities searched Bowman’s Mayodan residence and reportedly discovered evidence that intensified investigators’ interest.
September 30, 2002: Rockingham County, North Carolina, prosecutors obtained court authorization to subpoena Bowman’s telephone records.
October 4, 2002: Authorities publicly announced that Bowman was not a suspect, but said they wanted to interview him. Investigators had learned he was in Canada.
October 8, 2002: Authorities obtained a federal material-witness warrant for Bowman.
October 11, 2002: Canadian authorities ordered Bowman deported.
October 17, 2002: Canadian authorities released Bowman’s van and other items seized from his Inuvik apartment to the FBI. Canadian prosecutors also dropped charges against Bowman.
October 21, 2002: Bowman was deported to Raleigh, North Carolina, where FBI agents arrested him on the federal material-witness warrant. Investigators interviewed him for approximately four hours.
October 22, 2002: At a detention hearing in Roanoke, a federal magistrate described Bowman as a flight risk and ordered him held.
October 30, 2002: A federal prosecutor sought to have the material-witness warrant dismissed. Bowman was released and remained obligated to testify before the federal grand jury.
November 12, 2002: Bowman was scheduled to appear before the federal grand jury investigating the Short murders.
Michael operated M.S. Mobile Home Movers.
The business became an important investigative avenue because it created a large universe of:
Property owners
Business disputes
People whose mobile homes Michael moved
People Michael encountered while looking for work
Investigators continue seeking people whose mobile homes Michael moved in 2002 but who were never interviewed.
Michael and Mary were considering relocating.
Michael traveled through portions of South Carolina looking for employment. Those trips occurred during the spring and summer immediately preceding the murders.
Eight years later, investigators still considered those contacts important enough to conduct a multi-city interview operation.
Bennettsville
Myrtle Beach

No publicly identified South Carolina suspect has been charged.

The investigative focus is broader than any single historical person of interest. Authorities have repeatedly revisited preserved evidence, old interviews, business contacts, South Carolina leads, and the complete case file.
Beginning in 2021, a multi-agency task force examined preserved physical evidence for new forensic opportunities.
In 2023, another fresh-eyes task force received the entire case file for renewed review.
By 2025, evidence collected in 2002 had been submitted to DNA Labs International for advanced DNA testing, funded by the FBI.
Authorities have not publicly disclosed whether they have developed a complete unknown DNA profile or whether they are using forensic genetic genealogy.
One possibility is that Jennifer was the intended victim.
Under this theory, Michael and Mary may have been killed so the offender could abduct Jennifer without interference.
Jennifer’s removal from the residence supports consideration of this theory.
No publicly released evidence currently proves it.
Another possibility is that Michael was targeted because of a personal or business dispute.
The investigation into Michael’s mobile-home business, customers, and South Carolina activities demonstrates that law enforcement has considered his relationships an important avenue.
